findings.summary: the diff modifies imas_codex/search/fusion.py and tests/search/test_fusion.py, which the node's brief did not declare as write paths, so a reader comparing the diff against the brief sees two files outside the dispatched scope.

the manifest's negative_control.log names test_comparator_rerank_merges_item_orders_by_mean_rank, a test that no longer exists after the fuses-by-reciprocal-rank rename, so the red log's second failing id does not correspond to the head revision.

rerank_name_comparators returns a non-empty seat whenever model resolves even if no judgement call was made (every item's query empty), contradicting its docstring's "empty when no call was made"; harmless because the caller charges only when cost > 0, but the contract is unpinned by any test.

item_verdicts.call_sites: the rerank sits behind _reranked_nearby_comparators and _rerank_comparators_for_worker, reached by two production compose sites: imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:4032 (compose_worker) and imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:5897 (compose_batch).
item_verdicts.diff: read all ten commits c98a0d42..400416975 commit by commit; six files changed (fusion.py +51/-9, context.py +165, workers.py +142, test_fusion.py +33, test_comparator_rerank.py +414, the 114-line fragment), with the final commit 400416975 docs-only.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for a stubbed-decision reorder test that fails with the call removed, the off path byte-identical, a named citation of rerank_pool's failure-order test, and base/after suites with no added failure; tests/standard_names/test_comparator_rerank.py:73/110 supply the two arms, negative_control.log shows the reorder test red with the call removed (EXIT=1), the fragment cites test_rerank_pool_keeps_the_pool_order_when_every_judgement_fails at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-selection-over-generation/ssog-comparator-rerank.html:21, and the manifest records baseline_suite and after_suite with revision, exit_status and completed true.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to rerank the compose prompt's nearby-name comparator block through rerank_pool behind a single default-off switch; imas_codex/standard_names/context.py:1074 adds rerank_name_comparators and imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:1997 _rerank_comparators_for_compose, both reached only when comparator_rerank_enabled() (context.py:1037) is true, which reads IMAS_CODEX_SN_COMPOSE_RERANK_COMPARATORS and defaults off.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states the head gate (head_gate_r3.log, 845 passed/1 skipped/0 failed, EXIT=0 at bb2508c70) against the base arm (baseline_suite.log, 827 passed/1 skipped/0 failed, EXIT=0) and lists the negative controls.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the brief declared four paths (context.py, workers.py, tests/standard_names/test_comparator_rerank.py, the fragment), but the diff also modifies imas_codex/search/fusion.py and tests/search/test_fusion.py, which the node's own manifest declares as write paths but the brief does not.

justifications.durability: tests/standard_names/test_comparator_rerank.py:76 supplies a fixed order through a stubbed rerank_pool and asserts the returned order against a literal, so reverting the rerank call reddens it (negative_control.log, EXIT=1), while test_compose_worker_books_through_the_charging_helper at line 403 is a source-string check rather than a behavioural one.
justifications.evidence: the after arm head_gate_r3.log records 845 passed/1 skipped/EXIT=0 at the code head bb2508c70 against baseline_suite.log's 827/1/EXIT=0, and the reorder assertion at tests/standard_names/test_comparator_rerank.py:80 is shown red by negative_control.log, though the base arm ran a shorter file list than the head arm.
justifications.fit: workers.py:1997 repeats the sibling rerank callers' try/except (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:222, imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:206) with the same ranking-is-not-a-gate comment, and no plan, sprint or ticket label appears in the new names.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/standard_names/context.py:1074 reranks the comparator block per item through rerank_pool under the sn-judge seat and fuses the item orders, and both compose sites (workers.py:4032, :5897) gate it on the default-off switch, though the function returns a 3-tuple (ordered, cost, seat) where the two the brief asked for.
justifications.reuse: fusion.py:41 adds rrf_fuse_in_input_order beside its owner and extracts _rrf_mass so the two share arithmetic, rerank_pool is reused rather than re-implemented, and the spend is booked through BudgetManager.reserve/charge_event, so nothing the repository owns is forked.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff reaches imas_codex/search/fusion.py and tests/search/test_fusion.py, which the brief's declared write scope omits (the manifest declares them), the reuse repair a prior review defect required.
